title: When More Metadata Misleads: Probing Field-Level Grounding in LLM-Generated Museum Descriptions
abstract: arXiv:2610.31193v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Metadata-conditioned generation is often framed as a data-to-text task in which additional input fields should improve grounding. Museum description generation challenges this assumption because catalogue records are heterogeneous, partially visual, and unevenly documented across geographic regions. We study how metadata composition shapes the generation of artefact descriptions through a two-phase framework. Phase 1 analyses natural metadata variation in a large museum collection, where field count, field type, image availability, and Place co-vary. Phase 2 introduces controlled field probes that hold object identity fixed while varying metadata quantity, field type, and image access. Our results show that metadata quantity alone does not explain generation behaviour. Field type determines whether models ground, omit, or infer information, while images can both support visual grounding and increase unsupported interpretation. More broad

translated_title: 当更多元数据反而误导时：探查大语言模型生成的博物馆描述中的字段级接地性
translated_abstract: 元数据条件生成通常被视为一种数据到文本的任务，即更多的输入字段应当能改善生成内容的接地性（grounding）。然而博物馆描述生成对这一假设提出了挑战，因为馆藏目录记录具有异构性、部分依赖视觉信息，且在不同地理区域间的记录完备程度参差不齐。我们通过一个两阶段框架研究元数据的构成如何影响文物描述的生成。第一阶段分析了一个大型博物馆藏品中元数据的自然变化，其中字段数量、字段类型、图像可用性和地点等因素共同变化。第二阶段引入了受控的字段探针，在保持文物身份不变的前提下，改变元数据数量、字段类型和图像的访问情况。我们的结果表明，元数据数量本身并不能解释生成行为；字段类型才是决定模型对接地、省略还是推断信息的关键因素，而图像既能够支持视觉接地，也可能增加缺乏依据的解读。
tldr: 该研究通过两阶段实验发现，元数据数量本身并不能提升大语言模型生成博物馆文物描述的可靠性，真正决定模型是接地、省略还是凭空推断信息的是字段类型，而图像既能支持视觉接地也可能助长无依据的解读。
en_tdlr: This study shows through a two-phase framework that metadata quantity alone does not explain LLM generation behavior for museum artifact descriptions; field type determines whether models ground, omit, or infer information, while images can both support visual grounding and increase unsupported interpretation.
